draft.title: Negative fractions and decimals
card: The sign rules for integers work for fractions and decimals too. Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer.
Fractions
decide the sign first. Then multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms. For example, −1/2 × 3/4 = −3/8, because the signs are different.
Decimals
decide the sign first, then multiply as usual. For example, −0.5 × −0.4 = 0.2, because the signs are the same.
Division
the same sign rules apply. For example, −1.2 ÷ 0.3 = −4, because the signs are different.
draft.remember: Fractions and decimals follow the same sign rules as integers.

a.why: Both fractions are negative, so the answer is positive. 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 5 = 15, so the answer is 6/15, which simplifies to 2/5. The option −2/5 has the wrong sign.
a.clue: Check the signs, then multiply tops and bottoms.

b.why: The signs are different, so the answer is negative. 3.6 ÷ 0.9 = 4, so the answer is −4. The answer 4 has the wrong sign, and −0.4 puts the decimal point in the wrong place.

problems.detail: The clue says 'Different signs', which tells students the answer is negative before they apply the sign rule themselves. That leaves only −4 and −0.4, so the clue does the part of the question this point teaches. Question a's clue only says 'Check the signs', which is the better model.

proposal.title: Negative fractions and decimals
card: The sign rules for integers work for fractions and decimals too. Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer.
Fractions
decide the sign first. Then multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms and simplify if you can. For example, −1/2 × 3/4 = −3/8, because the signs are different.
Decimals
decide the sign first, then multiply as usual. For example, −0.5 × −0.4 = 0.2, because the signs are the same.
Division
the same sign rules apply. For example, −1.2 ÷ 0.3 = −4, because the signs are different and 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
proposal.remember: Fractions and decimals follow the same sign rules as integers.

a.why: Both fractions are negative, so the answer is positive. 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 5 = 15, so the answer is 6/15, which simplifies to 2/5. The option −2/5 has the wrong sign, and 10/9 comes from dividing instead of multiplying.
a.clue: Check the signs, then multiply tops and bottoms.

b.why: One number is negative and one is positive, so the answer is negative. 3.6 ÷ 0.9 is the same as 36 ÷ 9 = 4, so the answer is −4. The answer 4 has the wrong sign, and −0.4 puts the decimal point in the wrong place.
b.clue: Check the signs, then work out 36 ÷ 9.
